From form to CRM

SFMC config sends the submission. The integration code turns it into assigned CRM work.

How it works

Open a stage to see what lives in configuration and what lives in code.

A form submission follows three ownership boundaries

Form + SFMC settingsMarketing / SFMC owner

Owns fields, collection language and the automation that sends a submission. Ask the SFMC administrator for the business unit and editing permissions.

webhook request
Integration repositoryData engineering

Owns request validation, receipts, matching, routing and retry behavior. A repository change does not change SFMC settings.

record + owner
CRMCRM operations

Owns business routing decisions, queues and user access. Engineering writes through the agreed API contract.

Notification is a separate outcome

Saved opportunityCRM

The record and its assigned owner already exist.

delivery request
Notification serviceConnector / service owner

Delivers the alert. A failed alert requires retrying delivery, not creating a second opportunity.

Where a standard form-intake layer would fit

Form → retained submission and answers → downstream consumers. This would preserve reusable source records before CRM routing. It is a separate proposed capability, not another name for a webhook receiver.

Engineering owns integration behavior. SFMC administration, CRM roles, business routing, and connector consent remain separate responsibilities.

Rules and supporting detail

The handoff

Validate request
→
Save receipt
→
Match contact
→
Assign opportunity

The receiving endpoint checks authorization and required fields. It records the submission identity, matches or creates the contact, then creates an opportunity with a routing rule. A notification tells the assigned owner about the saved work.

BoundaryEvidence to keep
Form → receiverSubmission ID and validation result
Receiver → CRMReceipt linked to contact, opportunity, and owner
CRM → notificationDelivery attempt and final delivery status

When the last step fails

A failed notification does not erase a saved opportunity. Retry the incomplete step using the existing receipt. Replaying the entire submission without a stable identity can create duplicate records or notify the wrong owner.

What this browser demo actually does

The example keeps state in memory. It does not accept real form data, authenticate to a CRM, create records, or send messages. Reloading the page resets it.
